evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI explicitly acknowledged three named limitations more than a year before Marcus's post. The same section also reports reduced hallucination and improved factuality, so it supports unresolved problems rather than an absence of progress.

evidence_items.locator: Section 2.1, discussion of autonomous planning evaluations
evidence_items.explanation: The paper reports that approximately 12% of GPT-4-generated plans in the cited evaluations were executable and achieved their goals. It also discusses symbolic planners and hybrid approaches, limiting any inference that all forms of planning were unsolved.

This survey describes hallucination as a continuing deployment obstacle and reviews more than 32 mitigation techniques. It documents both persistent difficulty and active attempts to improve reliability.

evidence_items.locator: Private Investment Drops (But We See You, GenAI)
evidence_items.explanation: The section reports $25.2 billion invested in generative AI during 2023, nearly nine times the previous year's amount. This supports substantial contemporary capitalization, without claiming that investment remained equally large throughout earlier decades.

McCarthy's 1984 lecture describes expert systems' failures outside their intended scope and the difficulty of formalizing common-sense reasoning. The dated web version establishes a decades-long history for these general problems, although it does not document modern hallucination research over that entire period.

unresolved_gaps: The historical evidence establishes longstanding brittleness and reasoning difficulties, not a continuous history of every modern hallucination mechanism.
No finite benchmark collection establishes failure across every AI approach or every task.
